page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.mn4.8xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine built on KVM virtualization within the shared-core mn4 family. It is equipped with an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, delivering 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores via hyper-threading. The system includes 33 MB of L3 cache alongside instruction support for AVX, AVX-512F, and AES. The instance contains 128.0 GB of memory, establishing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. No local storage is attached to the hardware, requiring remote cloud storage volumes, and it lacks integrated GPU acceleration. Baseline network throughput is configured at 5 Gbps.

Benchmark results demonstrate a clear split between single-threaded and multi-threaded throughput. Due to moderate base clock frequencies, single-core benchmarks rank lower; Geekbench single-core reaches 952.0 and single-core stress-ng registers 1108.79, reflecting weak per-thread performance. Single-threaded gzip compression is notably limited at 19.06 GB/sec. Conversely, the 32 vCPUs yield solid middle-tier multi-core results, posting a PassMark CPU score of 28365.71, a Geekbench multi-core score of 8555.0, and 29386.71 in multi-core stress-ng. Memory bandwidth yields 128.57 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB reads and 51.27 GB/sec for uncached writes.

From an operational and resource-efficiency perspective, the shared CPU model provides substantial raw thread capacity and aggregate memory volume at a lower entry barrier than dedicated bare-metal or compute-intensive tiers. However, the shared nature and moderate clock speeds create performance tradeoffs for latency-sensitive applications. Workloads dependent on high single-core execution speeds or extensive local disk IOPS will encounter bottlenecks. Alibaba Cloud ecs.mn4.8xlarge is primarily suited for multi-threaded background processing, distributed batch jobs, intermediate-sized database operations, CI/CD compilation workloads, and static web serving.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.mn4.8xlarge is a general-purpose virtual instance featuring 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at 2.5 GHz on KVM virtualization. Configured with 128.0 GB of system memory, it adheres to a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. The instance includes no bundled local storage and has no GPU hardware, relying on external network storage alongside a 5 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmark data reflects moderate multi-core throughput, including a PassMark CPU score of 28365.71 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 8555.0, contrasted by lower single-thread efficiency (Geekbench single-core 952.0). Shared CPU resource allocation balances high-density concurrency against moderate per-core speeds, making it practical for multi-threaded compilation, backend web services, distributed batch computing, and caching layers like Redis.
